notes:
Lead source: self-serve signup (trial credits) from product page. Engineering lead: @Liam Park (CTO). Primary ask: hosted API that 'just works' during marketing spikes. Key themes below:

- Traffic profile: bursty inbound campaigns, short-lived spikes (3-10 minutes), 50-200 qps peaks during launches, baseline 2-5 qps.
- Problem observed: prototype using another provider hit repeated 429s during campaign test; they rate-limited on concurrency and short window quotas. Liam: "429s killed the demo — customers thought our product was flaky."
- What they want: predictable soft quotas for trial tier, clear header info (X-RateLimit-*) and retry-after guidance, optional short burst buffer to absorb spikes (30s-2m), and easy self-serve quota bump for paying customers.
- Cost sensitivity: SMB — wants low minimum spend, usage-based billing, but willing to pay for burst protection if it prevents lost demos.
- Technical constraints: public cloud only, prefer simple REST/SDK, no on-prem/VPC. SSO required for admin console (SAML).
- Model needs: small-to-medium chat model for customer-first responses during trials, embeddings for FAQ search, reranking for lead-priority sorting. Latency target: p95 < 400ms for chat on trial traffic; willing to accept higher tail during extreme bursts if graceful degradation occurs.
- Fallback strategy: eager to use lower-capacity model variant on overload (they mentioned "fallback to cheaper model during spikes"). Interested in automated routing by policy.
- Ops expectations: human-readable quota metrics in console, alerting when trial customers approach burst caps, and a simple way to request temporary burst increases through console or API.

Sales notes / tone: friendly, technical buyer; churn risk tied to first 2 demos. They signed up themselves and started experimenting — tester account currently throttled. Decision maker: Liam (CTO), influencer: Maya (Head of Product).
